steps.note: Open the single-stage event creation flow.
Set the event to a rank-based auction awarding the entire lot.
Provide the required event title.
Apply the first available auction pricing template so the product sheet is available.
Add the requested product as the first line with quantity 10.
Populate the required pricing-sheet fields.
Set the requested plant location on the first line item.
Verify the requested location was retained.
Commit the 30-minute schedule starting now.
Invite three QA vendors so the auction has Vendor A, B, and C participants.
Publish the configured auction.
Verify the event reached a real published project page.
Submit Vendor A's bid at 100.
Verify the first vendor's bid was accepted.
Submit Vendor B's lower bid at 95.
Verify the second vendor's bid was accepted.
Open the available QA vendor supplier-portal session for a vendor-side rank check.
Open this auction's pricing round in the vendor portal.
Verify the available vendor-side view exposes the expected rank after the competing lower bid, without asserting the competitor's price.

args.need: open a separate supplier-portal session as the second bidding vendor and verify that vendor sees Rank 1 without seeing the other vendor's price

steps.note: The catalog cannot create a second independent vendor session, which is required to check Vendor B's private view.
Return to the buyer console for buyer-side assertions.
Verify the buyer sees both direct vendor responses live.
Open the buyer's comparison grid to inspect the two live bid prices and ranks.
Verify two real vendor columns are shown to the buyer.
Verify the first vendor's bid price is visible to the buyer.
Verify the second vendor's bid price is visible to the buyer.
Verify the buyer-side ranks follow the lower bid, making 95 Rank 1 and 100 Rank 2.
